bylaws: Punishment late fee: if the loser does not complete the punishment by the start of the next draft, the loser must pay one extra buy-in, which goes into weekly payouts.

Champion's keeper, fully optional: the defending champion may keep one player from their roster. The kept player must be taken with a first-round pick, and since managers choose their own draft slots, a champion who keeps takes the last available slot and spends the final pick of round one on that player. Declining the keeper leaves the champion in the normal slot-selection order.

Offseason competitions set the draft-slot selection order. Each of the four bottom finishers is assigned a month - April, May, June, or July - and that manager decides their month's competition, which must be something every manager can easily take part in. Everyone's finishing rankings from the four competitions are averaged, and the final average ranking is the order in which managers choose their draft slots. Anyone who sits out a month ranks one place below the last manager who competed, so skipping always costs more than finishing last.
